classes.title: Lifecycle / snapshot-tagging / patch-currency hygiene
classes.definition: Lower-severity data-store operational hygiene: lifecycle configuration, copy-tags-to-snapshots, event notifications, and automatic minor-version upgrades.

classes.title: Backup / durability / deletion-protection gaps
classes.definition: Backup, retention, versioning, replication, deletion protection, Multi-AZ, backtracking or HA controls that protect data recoverability are absent.

classes.title: Data-store encryption at rest missing
classes.definition: The stored data of a persistence resource (S3, EBS, RDS/Aurora, Neptune, Elasticsearch, ECR) is not encrypted at rest at all, independent of which key is used.

classes.title: Weak encryption key ownership / rotation
classes.definition: Encryption exists but does not use a customer-managed KMS key, or the KMS key itself lacks rotation or a policy — a distinct property from whether data is encrypted at all.

classes.title: Data-store logging / audit gaps
classes.definition: Access logging, audit logging, or performance/enhanced monitoring is not enabled on a data store, reducing forensic and audit visibility.

classes.title: Data store publicly accessible
classes.definition: A storage resource is reachable from the public internet via a missing/disabled S3 public-access-block, public ACL/policy, or a publicly_accessible database flag.

classes.title: Data-store transport encryption weak or absent
classes.definition: A data store accepts plaintext connections or uses an outdated TLS policy for client/node traffic (RDS in-transit, Elasticsearch HTTPS/node-to-node/TLS).

classes.title: Security-group documentation hygiene
classes.definition: Security groups or their rules lack descriptions — a documentation/maintainability check with no direct exposure impact.

classes.title: Unrestricted outbound egress
classes.definition: A security group rule allows unrestricted egress to any destination, creating a data-exfiltration path (a distinct property from inbound exposure).

classes.title: Network flow / access logging gaps
classes.definition: VPC flow logging or load-balancer access logging is disabled, reducing network-level visibility.

classes.title: Unrestricted inbound exposure
classes.definition: A security group, cluster endpoint, or load balancer accepts inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 or an open CIDR, exposing an attack surface to the internet.

classes.title: Weak network isolation / segmentation
classes.definition: A resource is not placed behind proper network boundaries: default SG not locked down, subnets auto-assign public IPs, resource not in a VPC, uses the default SG, or pods lack a NetworkPolicy.

classes.title: Load-balancer / listener transport encryption
classes.definition: A network front-end (ELB) terminates or forwards traffic without TLS/SSL or without an ACM-provided certificate.

classes.title: Identity & authentication controls
classes.definition: Identity is managed weakly: direct user policies instead of SSO/groups, no instance profile/role attachment, or database IAM authentication disabled.

classes.title: Hardcoded credentials & secret exposure
classes.definition: Access keys, secrets, or high-entropy strings are embedded in provider config, EC2 user data, Lambda env, or Kubernetes manifests.

classes.title: Over-permissive / wildcard permissions
classes.definition: An IAM policy or Kubernetes RBAC role grants wildcard actions/resources, unconstrained write/permission-management, or broad principals rather than least privilege.

classes.title: Privilege escalation & sensitive-permission paths
classes.definition: A policy or binding enables privilege escalation, credential exposure, data exfiltration, cluster-admin, or reading all secrets — permission shapes that are dangerous beyond mere breadth.

classes.title: Instance metadata service hardening
classes.definition: An EC2 instance permits IMDSv1 (no required session tokens), exposing instance-role credentials to SSRF-style theft.

classes.title: Managed orchestration control-plane hardening
classes.definition: An IaC-provisioned managed cluster (EKS) has control-plane logging disabled or secrets encryption off at the cluster level.

classes.title: Compute reliability & observability gaps
classes.definition: Lower-severity operational hardening: detailed instance monitoring, EBS optimization, Lambda dead-letter queue, concurrency limit, or X-Ray tracing not configured.

classes.title: Workload integrity & patch currency
classes.definition: A compute workload lacks code-signing validation, runs a deprecated runtime, or leaves environment secrets unencrypted — integrity/supply-chain and patching properties.

classes.title: Host isolation / breakout surface
classes.definition: A workload shares host PID/IPC/network namespaces, mounts the Docker socket or hostPath volumes, or automounts service-account tokens — paths toward container escape or host compromise.

classes.title: Image provenance & supply chain
classes.definition: A workload uses a mutable/latest image tag, no image digest, or an untrusted registry, weakening image provenance guarantees.

classes.title: Registry image vulnerability scanning
classes.definition: Registry-side CVE scanning of pushed images is disabled (ECR scan-on-push) - a vulnerability-detection property distinct from image provenance.

classes.title: Excess Linux capabilities
classes.definition: A container adds Linux capabilities (including NET_RAW) or fails to drop the default capability set to a least-privilege baseline.

classes.title: Privileged / root container execution
classes.definition: A container runs privileged, allows privilege escalation, runs as root or a low UID/GID, binds privileged ports, or (in a Dockerfile) declares no non-root user.

classes.title: Missing security-context hardening
classes.definition: A container omits a read-only root filesystem, a seccomp profile, an explicit securityContext, or file-based secret mounting.

classes.title: Workload resource-limit & hygiene gaps
classes.definition: Lower-severity workload hygiene: unset CPU/memory requests or limits, missing liveness/readiness probes, use of the default namespace, or no Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK.
